title: DONKEY CLIMB
oneLiner: Two Marios race up the girders, dodge rolling barrels, and rescue Pauline together.
mechanics: Exactly two players cooperate on the same full-screen arena, each controlling a separate Mario avatar with independent lives and score; they do not block one another physically.

Each stage contains five sloped girders linked by eight ladders. Move left/right along a girder; press up/down only while aligned with a usable ladder to climb; press A to jump, with held A producing a higher jump and a tap producing a short hop.

Donkey Kong visibly telegraphs each throw, then releases rolling barrels from the upper-left. Barrels roll downhill, bounce to the next girder at edges, and sometimes choose a usable ladder; later stages add fire hazards from the oil drum.

Jumping over each unique barrel awards 100 points once per player. Reaching each new floor awards 100 points once per player. Either player reaching Pauline's top-right rescue goal clears the stage and awards that player the remaining time bonus plus 1000; the stage-clear bonus is awarded to both players.

The three stages use the foundation's tested layouts, route guarantees, hazard cadence, and bounded speed escalation. Stage 1 teaches movement, ladders, and jumping; stage 2 increases barrel cadence and introduces fire; stage 3 combines the established hazards without exceeding tested limits.

Each life has a 100-second timer and the visible stage bonus begins at 5000, decaying in hundreds with elapsed time. Timer expiry costs one life. A barrel, fire, or fall also costs one life and triggers a death animation, then respawns that player at the highest floor reached with temporary protection.

Players may act immediately during any countdown; movement and jumping are practice-enabled while damage is suppressed until the round begins. A player reaching zero lives is revived with one life when the teammate clears a stage; otherwise all available lives exhausted loses the game.
Rescuing Pauline on stage 3 produces cooperative victory. START and cabinet lifecycle handle reset; no hammer, lift, rivet, cage, or original Donkey Kong topology is added.
artDirection: Compose the fixed 256x224 playfield around five brightly outlined sloped construction girders and eight ladders, with the top 12 pixels reserved for the runtime HUD. Use the bundled source sprites: Mario avatars are compact 16x20-class figures with distinct P1/P2 markers, red cap and overalls, readable idle, walking, climbing, jumping, hurt, and death poses; their physical collision body remains approximately 8x16. Pauline is a clearly contrasting 16x16 target at the top-right with pink dress and light hair, alternating waiting and rescued poses. Donkey Kong occupies roughly 40x40 at the upper-left with broad brown silhouette and visible idle/throw poses. Barrels are about 12x12, strongly circular and striped, with rolling and falling frames; fire hazards are about 16x16 with bright animated flame frames. Use the default 16-colour arcade palette with exact bundled source-sprite colours where supplied; keep girders, ladders, hazards, and characters high-contrast against a dark construction-site background. Broken secondary ladders, oil drum, girder supports, and sparse skyline details establish the setting without obscuring barrel paths or player silhouettes.

preserve: Mario climbs five sloped construction girders using ladders to reach Pauline at the top-right.
Donkey Kong stands above the course and telegraphs rolling barrels.
Barrels roll downhill, bounce at edges, sometimes descend ladders, and hazards include oil-drum fire on later stages.
Three-stage rescue progression, stage timer, lives, floor bonuses, jump-over-barrel scoring, and cooperative climber rules.
change: Use the available inspected source sprites for Mario, Pauline, Donkey Kong, barrels, and hazards.
Use the tested three-stage climber foundation rather than original arcade level topology or ROM behavior.
Make the game exactly two-player cooperative: both players are Mario climbers, either can reach Pauline, and both share stage-clear progression.

controls.left: Move left along the current girder
controls.right: Move right along the current girder
controls.up: Climb upward when aligned with a ladder
controls.down: Climb downward when aligned with a ladder
controls.a: Jump; hold for a higher jump, tap for a short hop

lose: The team loses when both players have exhausted their available lives before completing all three stages.
scoring: Earn 100 for each new floor, 100 for each unique barrel jumped per player, and rescue points plus the decaying time bonus when either player reaches Pauline; stage-clear bonuses go to both players.
